references.text: Both verses deal with distinguishing between the clean and the unclean, emphasizing the importance of remaining separate from impurity.
Moses exhorts the children of Israel to distinguish between the clean and the unclean, and to remain holy before the Lord.
The command to send unclean persons out of the camp so as not to defile the sanctuary parallels the warning in Leviticus 15:31.
Anyone who makes the Lord's tabernacle unclean by failing to cleanse themselves shall be cut off from Israel.
The warning that anyone who defiles the sanctuary shall be cut off corresponds to the death penalty mentioned in Leviticus 15:31.
Ezekiel describes how Israel defiled the sanctuary with their abominations, which connects to the warning about making the tabernacle unclean.
Israel has made the Lord's sanctuary unclean, reflecting the same concern expressed in Leviticus 15:31.
The Lord's dwelling (mishkan) shall be in the midst of the people, connecting to the phrase 'my dwelling which is among them' in Leviticus 15:31.
Paul exhorts believers to separate themselves from impurity because they are God's temple, reflecting the principle of keeping God's dwelling clean.
The warning to ensure that no one becomes a root of uncleanness that can defile many is linked to the theme of remaining pure.
